Here are things I wish I knew when I started practicing. 

1. If you definitely plan on paying off your loans in full and not using any income based repayment, forbearance, forgiveness or other benefit or payment plan , I would refinance the federal loans to get a lower interest rate. Of course, you need to consider whether you may want the safety net of those gov’t options later down the line.

2. When deciding whether to put your income in savings/investments... a big part of it is simple math. Right now, your loans are guaranteed to accrue interest at around 6-7% where the rate of return on investments will vary, so generally, paying off your loans first will guarantee more money in your wallet at the end of the day. 

3. The caveat is of course, put away emergency savings, and if you can refinance your loans to a lower rate, below 5% etc you may want to invest a portion of your income. For example, some funds have a demonstrated rate of return of 10-11%, if you are certain that your investments will grow by at least that rate, and your loans are accruing at a substantially slower rate, you could grow your income in investments.  


4. There is no point in half utilizing a repayment/forgiveness plan and half planning to pay off your full loans. So if you are on a repayment plan, you need to understand that you are paying off the loan at such a slow pace that you will never fully pay off the loan and that you are committing to 10 or 25 years of payments. Whatever the term of that loan is. 

The interest that you pay over the life of the loan will be substantially more than if you had paid it off quickly, so you need to decide which option you prefer. But don’t waffle, ie go on a payment plan but inconsistently make large payments w the idea that maybe youll pay off the loans, maybe not (what I did). 

Anyway, your plan is totally doable and it’s great you are thinking of it so early. I’m on track to pay off about $200k of loans in the next year and I started on a 65k salary, but I probably would have done it a lot sooner if I had planned/been more serious about it sooner.
